elements.html: BikeTO
Bike directions for Toronto that favour bike lanes, with Bike Share, bike parking and the TTC built in.
Free on the App Store · No account, no ads, no tracking

BikeTO guiding a Bike Share ride with the time left on the pass

slides.notes: Introduce BikeTO: a free iPhone app for turn-by-turn bike navigation in Toronto, with Bike Share, bike parking and the TTC built in. Goal for today: show what BikeTO does, and ask whether there is a way to work together.

slides.name: The gap

elements.html: WHY I BUILT BIKETO
A bike trip in Toronto often takes several apps

01

Bike lanes come second

General map apps don’t make it easy to choose bike lanes over busy roads, or show how much of a route is on a bike lane.

02

One trip, three apps

A rider might find a bike in the Bike Share app, plan the route in a maps app and check the TTC in a third.

03

Surprises on the way

Pass time running out, a full dock or nowhere to lock up can come as a surprise on the way.
BikeTO tries to put the whole trip in one app, using Toronto’s open data.

slides.notes: Frame the rider’s experience today. Every Bike Share trip involves picking a bike, a route, maybe the TTC, and a dock. Today that is spread across apps, and the stressful moments (full docks, pass time) happen mid-ride.

slides.name: BikeTO at a glance

elements.html: BIKETO 2.0 AT A GLANCE
What BikeTO does

Pick your streets

Bike lanes only, or bike lanes plus quiet neighbourhood roads.

Built for Bike Share

Live bikes and docks, a pass countdown, and a new station if yours fills up.

Bike + Transit

Ride to the subway or bring your bike on board, with live TTC departures.

Turn-by-turn

Spoken directions, rerouting and a Live Activity on the Lock Screen.

Ready to park

Own-bike trips end at a bike parking spot, with rack type and spaces.

Private by design

No account, no ads, no tracking. Settings stay on the phone.

elements.altText: BikeTO turn-by-turn guidance with the next turn and arrival time

slides.notes: Six things BikeTO 2.0 does today. The next four slides look closer at the ones most related to Bike Share.

slides.name: Riders choose their streets

elements.html: FEATURE 1 OF 4
Riders choose their streets

• Two route styles. Bike lanes only, or bike lanes plus quiet neighbourhood roads.
  • Bike-lane share on every route. Riders see, for example, 93% vs 88% on bike lanes before they go.
  • A clear trade-off. BikeTO says how much time the other route saves, such as “Saves 6 min”.
  • Their favourite first. The rider’s preferred route style is always listed on top.

How it could help Bike Share riders

New and occasional riders can pick routes they feel comfortable on, which may help them ride again.

elements.altText: Route options to Christie Pits Park: 32 minutes on bike lanes only, or 26 minutes with neighbourhood roads
The faster neighbourhood-roads route selected, saving 6 minutes with 88% on bike lanes

slides.notes: Routes are built from the City of Toronto cycling network merged into OpenStreetMap, with gaps in the bike lane network repaired, so the bike-lane percentage is real.

slides.name: Made for Bike Share trips

elements.html: FEATURE 2 OF 4
Made for Bike Share trips

• Walk to a station with bikes. Live bike and e-bike counts from Bike Share Toronto’s station feed.
  • Pass countdown. Time left on the pass stays on screen, and on the Lock Screen, while riding.
  • Full dock on the way. If the destination station fills up on the way, BikeTO reroutes to the next one and says why.
  • Ends at a free dock. Trips finish at a station with open docks, then walk the last few metres.

How it could help Bike Share riders

Could help riders avoid overtime fees and full docks, two common frustrations.

elements.altText: A Bike Share ride showing 18 minutes left on the pass
BikeTO switching to Queen St W / Bathurst St because Bloor St W / Shaw St is full

slides.notes: This is the feature set built specifically for Bike Share riders. The station-full switch uses the live station feed while the rider is moving.

slides.name: Bike + Transit, and a place to park

elements.html: FEATURE 3 OF 4
Bike + Transit, and a place to park

• Bike and ride. Ride to a subway station, park, and take the TTC, with live departures.
  • Bike on board. Knows the TTC’s rules, such as no bikes on the subway at weekday rush hour, and plans around them.
  • TTC, then Bike Share. Connects the last part of a trip from a station to a Bike Share dock.
  • Ready to park. Own-bike trips end at a City bike parking spot, with rack type and spaces.

How it could help Bike Share riders

Shows Bike Share as a way to cover the first and last kilometre of TTC trips.

elements.altText: A bike-and-ride trip that parks at the station because bikes are not allowed on the subway at rush hour
A trip that takes the TTC to Union Station, then Bike Share for the last part
Arriving at a ring-and-post bike parking spot with 2 spaces at 750 Bloor St W

slides.notes: Transit trips come from OpenTripPlanner with the TTC GTFS feed, so departures and stops are the TTC’s own schedule.

slides.name: Turn-by-turn guidance, even when locked

elements.html: FEATURE 4 OF 4
Turn-by-turn guidance, even when locked

• Spoken directions. A banner for the next turn and a step list for the whole trip.
  • Rerouting. Miss a turn and BikeTO finds a new way.
  • Lock Screen and Dynamic Island. The trip keeps going with the phone locked, through a Live Activity.
  • A map for cyclists. Bike lanes, Bike Share stations with live counts, bike parking and repair shops.

How it could help Bike Share riders

Spoken directions help riders keep their eyes on the road. A phone mount on Bike Share bikes could help further.

elements.altText: Turn-by-turn guidance: in 150 metres, turn left onto Bay West Teamway
The next turn shown as a Live Activity on the iPhone Lock Screen

slides.notes: Riders should not be looking at their phone while riding. Spoken directions and the Lock Screen Live Activity mean they rarely need to. This sets up the phone mount idea in the ask.

slides.name: How it works

elements.html: HOW IT WORKS
Built on Toronto’s open data

City of Toronto Open Data

Cycling network and bike parking

OpenStreetMap

Every street and path in Toronto

Bike Share Toronto

Live station feed: bikes and docks

TTC

Schedules for subway, streetcar and bus

BikeTO routing on Google Cloud

  • Merges the City’s cycling network into the map and repairs gaps between bike lanes
  • Scores every street by its bike infrastructure for the two route styles
  • Joins bike legs with TTC trips, including the TTC’s bikes-on-board rules
  • Watches live Bike Share counts to switch full stations

elements.altText: BikeTO app icon

elements.html:
BikeTO on iPhone

Version 2.0 on the App Store. No account, no ads, no tracking: settings stay on the phone.

slides.notes: For anyone who asks how reliable it is: BikeTO runs its own routing servers (GraphHopper for bikes, OpenTripPlanner for transit) built from public data, refreshed regularly. Nothing depends on a rider account.

slides.name: Why it matters

elements.html: HOW IT COULD HELP BIKE SHARE TORONTO
Better trips could mean more rides

More confident riders

Routes that favour bike lanes and quiet streets may help new riders try Bike Share, and come back.

Fewer surprises

Pass countdowns and full-dock rerouting can help riders avoid overtime fees and full stations.

Connected to transit

Bike Share can cover the first and last kilometre of TTC trips, planned in one place.

Available today, for free

BikeTO 2.0 is on the App Store and built on open data, with no ads and no tracking.

slides.notes: How BikeTO might support Bike Share’s goals: ridership, rider safety and satisfaction, and connections with transit.

slides.name: Phone mount concept

elements.html: CONCEPT RENDER
An idea: a phone mount for Bike Share bikes

elements.altText: Concept render: an iPhone showing BikeTO turn-by-turn directions, held in a green four-corner cradle on a tilt joint, clamped to a bike handlebar beside the stem

elements.html:
Tool-free clamp

Fits beside the stem, with no changes to the bike.

Four-corner cradle

Spring-loaded corners hold most phones, with or without a case.

Tilt joint

Angles the screen toward the rider, so a glance is enough.

With spoken directions and Lock Screen guidance, a mount could help riders keep their eyes on the road.

A concept render for illustration. The 3D designs could be prototyped together with Bike Share.

elements.title: 1. Tool-free clamp
elements.html:
Wraps the handlebar beside the stem and closes with a quick-release lever, so it goes on and comes off in seconds without tools.

Design notes

  • Rubber-lined jaws grip firmly without scratching the bar
  • Sits clear of the bell, brake levers and basket
  • Nothing on the bike is drilled or replaced

To work out with Bike Share

  • Handlebar sizes on each bike model, including e-bikes
  • Whether mounts stay on the bikes or riders bring their own

elements.title: 2. Four-corner cradle
elements.html:
Four spring-loaded corners hold the phone by its edges, so one design fits most phones, with or without a case.

Design notes

  • Open sides keep the buttons, charging port and camera free
  • Padded corners soften bumps from potholes and streetcar tracks
  • One hand to put the phone in and take it out

To work out with Bike Share

  • Which phone sizes to support
  • Ride tests on rough Toronto streets

elements.title: 3. Tilt joint
elements.html:
A ball joint between the arm and the cradle angles the screen toward the rider and holds it there.

Design notes

  • Tilts for riders of different heights
  • Turns for portrait or landscape
  • Firm enough to stay put over bumps

To work out with Bike Share

  • Readability in bright sun and glare
  • Durability for a fleet that lives outdoors all year

slides.notes: A concept render of the phone attachment for Bike Share bikes: a tool-free clamp beside the stem, a four-corner cradle and a tilt joint. It shows the idea; the 3D designs could be prototyped together with Bike Share. This is part of the next best case on the following slide. slides.name: The ask

elements.html: HOW WE COULD WORK TOGETHER
Three options, from most to least involved
BEST CASE

Integrate bike scanning into BikeTO

Riders could scan a Bike Share bike in BikeTO to unlock it, then go straight into navigation, pass tracking and docking.

 

This would need access to Bike Share’s rental and unlock system, and member sign-in.
NEXT BEST CASE

Bring BikeTO’s features into the Bike Share app

Work with Bike Share’s team to bring bike-lane routing, turn-by-turn guidance, pass countdowns and full-dock rerouting into the official app.

 

Plus 3D designs for phone mounts on Bike Share bikes, for hands-free directions.
ALTERNATIVE CASE

Partner app for safe bike navigation

Bike Share could mention BikeTO as a partner app that helps Toronto cyclists find safer routes.

 

For example in the Bike Share app, website, newsletters, social media or at stations.

slides.notes: Three options, from most to least involved. Best case: scanning and unlocking Bike Share bikes inside BikeTO. Next best: bring BikeTO features into the Bike Share app, plus 3D-designed phone mounts for the bikes. Alternative: mention BikeTO as a partner app. Ask which, if any, they would like to explore, and who to follow up with.
